page: Microsoft Azure EC2as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processor, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core across two hardware threads. The compute configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is set to 16.0 GB RAM, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-heavy small-scale services. The instance features no local disk storage, relying entirely on remote storage volumes, and includes no dedicated hardware GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight an emphasis on memory density rather than multithreaded raw compute throughput. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU throughput reached 1982.68, placing it in the average tier, while multi-core performance registered the same score of 1982.68, placing in the bottom 10 percent due to the two-vCPU hardware ceiling. Similarly, Geekbench returned an average single-core score of 1164.0, but a multi-core score of 1413.0, reflecting constrained aggregate processor capacity. Memory performance on PassMark registered at 1469.98, while Redis SET operations yielded 1.63 million operations per second, both sitting in the lower performance tiers.

Architecturally, the server provides dedicated CPU allocation alongside hardware acceleration flags such as AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and AVX, though advanced vector sets like AVX-512 and AMX are absent. The lack of integrated local storage necessitates architectural reliance on Azure Premium Storage or standard managed network disks. The qualitative cost profile makes this configuration efficient for environments that need moderate memory capacity at low resource overhead without paying for excessive CPU cores.

The Azure EC2as_v5 is suited for light in-memory caching nodes, staging instances for relational databases, Redis key-value stores, and microservices requiring an elevated RAM-to-CPU ratio without sustained multi-core compute pressure.
